title: Gratitude While You Wait
excerpt: Thankful before the story is finished. Generous with what you’ve received. Waiting on what God said He will do. This week, Thanksgiving turned toward Advent.
author: TheWrkShop Team
seo_title: Gratitude While You Wait: Weekend 4-3-2-1 | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Four Scriptures, three insights, two questions and one action step on gratitude in hard times, generosity and waiting on God as Advent begins.
body_html: What an unfinished year, an open table and the start of Advent taught us this week

This week we came to the table from five sides. Gratitude when life is unfinished. Gratitude that becomes generosity. Gratitude that becomes a way of living. A prayer for the table. And on Friday, the season turned: gratitude remembers, Advent waits.
This week was about gratitude while waiting on God: thanking Him before the story is finished, and letting what you received keep moving.
Gratitude does not require a finished story.

One-Minute Win of the Week
This weekend, ask someone you love: “What’s one thing God did for you this year?” Go first.

Thursday night. The plates are cleared, but one man stays at the table. The financial pressure he prayed about all year hasn’t lifted. He didn’t pretend otherwise when he prayed over the meal. He thanked God anyway, for what is true. He asked the table what God did for them this year, and he went first. The neighbor who would have been alone was sitting with them. Tomorrow the shopping lists come out. He’s starting a different list: what he’s waiting on God for, and what he’s been telling himself the wait means.

“Though the fig tree does not bud and there are no grapes on the vines, though the olive crop fails and the fields produce no food, though there are no sheep in the pen and no cattle in the stalls, yet I will rejoice in the LORD, I will be joyful in God my Savior.”
Insight: Gratitude is not always a response to changed circumstances. Sometimes it is trust in the middle of unchanged ones.
Gem: Thanksgiving and lament can exist in the same prayer.
“You will be enriched in every way so that you can be generous on every occasion, and through us your generosity will result in thanksgiving to God.”
Insight: The gift does not stop with the person who receives it. It moves outward.
Gem: What you received may be exactly what another person now needs.
“And whatever you do, whether in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.”
Insight: Gratitude is not merely something we express. It can become how we live.
Gem: Gratitude is not the center. Christ is.
“I wait for the LORD, my whole being waits, and in his word I put my hope. I wait for the Lord more than watchmen wait for the morning, more than watchmen wait for the morning.”
Insight: Gratitude remembers what God has done. Advent waits for what God has said He will do.
Gem: What we agree with in the waiting is what we bring to the arrival.
• Gratitude doesn’t wait for the answer. Without realizing it, we can make our gratitude depend on God doing what we expect.
• The loudest thank-you. What we do with what we’ve received is the loudest thank-you we’ll ever say.
• Waiting is a trigger. A delay always asks what it means. “God forgot.” “It’s all on me.” Those aren’t facts. They’re interpretations.
• Am I trusting God’s character, or only the outcome I hope He provides?
• What have I received that someone else now needs?

Pray it honestly: Name one unresolved burden. Tell God honestly how it affects you. Ask for what you want. Then name one truth about His character you can thank Him for. Don’t force an emotion. Practice honest prayer.
Wednesday traced the movement that forms a man:

Gratitude enters early. We notice gifts we used to overlook. We remember God’s faithfulness. Waiting enters early too. A delay asks what it means, and whatever we agree with in the waiting is what we bring to the arrival.
Want to trace it upstream in your own life? Walk through the Upstream Formation Framework.

Prayer
Father, You know what remains unresolved. Help me thank You without pretending my pain is gone. Teach me to trust Your character while I wait for answers. Thank You for every gift You have entrusted to me. May what I receive become a blessing beyond me. Teach me to receive with humility, remember with gratitude, give with generosity, and live in obedience to Christ. As this season turns, teach me to wait on what You have said You will do. Show me what I have been telling myself the waiting means, and give me the courage to agree with You instead. In Jesus’ name, amen.

Declaration
I will thank God before my story is finished. I will keep the gift moving and wait on what He said He will do.

Challenge: Advent begins Sunday. Take a moment and name what you’re waiting on God for this year. Don’t fix it. Don’t explain it. Just name it. Then ask: “What have I been telling myself this wait means?” Starting Tuesday, December 1: Advent with TheWrkShop. Every day through Christmas.
